newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Samancor shares up despite poor H1 results.
newsitem.headline: Samancor shares up despite poor H1 results.

text.p: Shares in ferro-alloy producer Samancor Ltd rose on Tuesday shrugging off a set of poor results for the six months to end December released on Monday.
Dealers said the extended commissioning problems at Samancor's Columbus Stainless joint-venture and low base metal prices in 1996 had been widely expected to dull the company's performance.
Strong prospects for a recovery this year boosted shares.
"The market has discounted the results because there are good recovery prospects in the second half. Manganese and chrome prices are picking up," one dealer said.
Traders said base metal stocks would benefit in the future as players shifted portfolios out of gold stocks, vulnerable following the persistent weakness in the bullion price.
"The share is expected to pick up generally because of the shift from golds towards metals. Metals offer safer returns than the golds which continue to be low," another trader said.
By 1235 GMT Samancor stocks were up 75 cents at 53.25 rand on volume of 13,300 shares.
Samancor on Monday released first half results showing attributable income plunging to 171.43 million from 381.92 million rand for the same period in 1995.
It reported earnings per share of 90 cents, down from 201 before, and a dividend of 30 cents down from 60.
Dealers said despite a brighter outlook for Samancor's shares a stronger rand, which dampens firms' export potential, may hem in future gains.
The rand was last trading at 4.4470 bid against the dollar, having this year improved from below the 4.70 level at the beginning of the year.
